patch_description: Expert insight: for n=26 in a unit square, the optimal packing is close to a hexagonal (triangular) lattice with defect rows near the walls, so the hex-rows seed is by far the strongest basin — but starting all four runs from exact lattice positions makes the annealer rediscover the same trajectory. Following the recommendation, I (1) jitter each start's centers with a small Gaussian perturbation (different seed per start) to decorrelate basins while keeping the strong base layout, (2) bias the annealer's moves toward circles that are "tight" (small radii / active constraints) since those have the most slack to gain, and (3) shrink the per-start step budget gracefully and give the hex seed extra steps. This directly extends the mechanism that produced the best score this round at negligible runtime cost.
